whatItFakes: With fast-forward on (development only), candidates take no campaign turns and volunteers walk no doors, so a race is decided by the voters' leans, parties, the incumbent's record and the impressions earlier days left.
why: The owner asked for 20 years in seconds, accepted if the result makes sense in the end (Nov 8, 1:58 a.m.); a campaign's town halls, speeches and doors are most of an election year's time.
replacement: A coarse campaign that moves each voter group's standing by the campaign's spending and reach, as counted groups are read, so the aggregate effect of a campaign remains.

whatItFakes: Another state's legislators are recorded husks until something opens them, and a husk has no health record, so none of them dies, falls ill or retires between elections (vacancies from outside deaths: 19 against 149 over two years in Dickey, North Dakota, seed n8g7).
why: Building 6,700 full people at the opening made 43 percent of a small town's year (owner, Nov 5: generate on demand); the death of a person nobody has opened needs the health engine's death path run for a husk.
replacement: Each husk official gets the same hazard profile and seeded line the health engine gives a person, a death day is booked on a due-date index, and on that day the person is built and dies through the health engine's own path, so the vacancy and special election follow.
